title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. X/S is a smooth curve over a base of characteristic 0. The previous page described, purely algebraically, a P^1-bundle P = P(E) with section σ and relative connection c. Here E is the extension 0→ω→E→O_X→0 given by E ≅ J/J^3 ⊗ ω^{-1}, with J the augmentation ideal of P^∞_{X/S}.

This page draws the conclusion. The possible structures of this type on X correspond bijectively to the lifts to order 3 of the order-2 datum p_(2), with no further condition on the lifts. Two such lifts differ by a section of Hom(ω, ω^{⊗3}) ≅ ω^{⊗2}. So the structures are the sections of a canonical torsor C_{X/S} under ω^{⊗2} = (Ω^1_{X/S})^{⊗2}. G. names this the torsor of 'projective connections' on X/S.

He then gives an equivalent description in the language of connections. Projective connections correspond to suitable connections on P = P(E), or equivalently on its associated Lie algebra bundle.
- That bundle is V = π_*T_{P/X} = E⊗Ě/O_X = End^0(E) ≅ Sym^2E ⊗ ω^{-1}, since det E = ω.
- V is a successive extension with graded pieces ω, O, ω^{-1}.
- A connection is c: V → V⊗ω ≅ Sym^2 E.
- Condition: on the subbundle ω ⊂ V, c must land in Ker(Sym^2E → Sym^2 O_X = O_X). That kernel is an extension of ω by ω^2.
- On the next page this extension is identified with P^1_{X/S}(ω), and c|_ω is required to equal the universal first-order operator d^1: ω → P^1(ω).
- The indeterminacy is then again ω⊗Ω^1 = ω^{⊗2}, consistent with the torsor description ('on retombe sur ses pattes').

In modern terms these are sl_2-opers (Gunning's indigenous bundles), and the torsor is the affine space of projective structures modelled on quadratic differentials (the Schwarzian derivative).

Purpose. Over C, the transcendental uniformization gives a canonical section of this torsor. G. then asks when it has logarithmic or regular singularities at infinity, i.e. at the cusps, presumably in connection with Gauss–Manin / Picard–Fuchs equations.
errors: 'torseur canonique sur S' should be a torsor on X (a sheaf on X whose sections over X are the structures). This is likely a slip, or a misreading of 'sur X'.
No mathematical errors otherwise. The identifications End^0(E) ≅ Sym^2E⊗(det E)^{-1}, the gradings ω, O, ω^{-1}, Hom(ω, ω^3) ≅ ω^2, and Ker(Sym^2E→O) as an extension of ω by ω^2 are all correct.

ideas.what: Projective structures on a curve form a torsor under quadratic differentials ω^{⊗2}, defined algebraically via P^∞_{X/S} (order-3 lifts of order-2 jet data).
ideas.modern_name: Torsor/affine space of projective structures (Schwarzian derivative)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Schwarz, Poincaré); Gunning (1966–67); algebraic relative versions by Ihara (1974) and Mochizuki (1990s)

ideas.what: Projective connection as a P^1-bundle P(E), E = J/J^3⊗ω^{-1} an extension of O by ω, with section and connection satisfying a transversality condition.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Gunning (indigenous bundles, 1967); Beilinson–Drinfeld (opers); Mochizuki (p-adic Teichmüller theory)

ideas.what: Oper condition on the adjoint bundle V = End^0(E) ≅ Sym^2E⊗ω^{-1}: the connection restricted to ω ⊂ V equals the universal operator d^1: ω → P^1(ω).
ideas.modern_name: sl_2-oper condition, formulated via principal parts

ideas.what: Question whether the canonical (uniformization) projective connection has logarithmic or regular singularities at the cusps.
ideas.modern_name: Regular singularity / unipotent monodromy of the Fuchsian uniformizing oper at punctures
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Poincaré, Fuchsian uniformization); Deligne 1970 for regular singularities in general

missed.claim: An early (c. 1972) algebraic, relative-over-S formulation of projective connections and opers via the principal parts ring P^∞_{X/S}, with the bundle E = J/J^3⊗ω^{-1}. It is placed in a dossier on Gauss–Manin connections and the Cartier operation. This prefigures the p-curvature / Cartier-operation study of indigenous bundles (Ihara, Mochizuki), but no new result is stated on this page.
missed.quote: Ce sont donc les sections sur X d'un torseur canonique ... faisceau abélien Hom(ω, ω^{⊗3}) ≃ ω^{⊗2} ... torseur des "connexions projectives"
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: Grothendieck was handling the oper/indigenous-bundle formalism in a Gauss–Manin/Cartier context years before Mochizuki's p-adic Teichmüller theory.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is the classical theory of projective structures and indigenous bundles, recast in Grothendieck's principal-parts language. It is correct and elegant but standard. The only interest is historical: the early date and the Cartier-operation context, which anticipates Ihara and Mochizuki.
transcription_corrections: '(i.e. qui divise P → X de V_{P/X}' should likely read '(i.e. image directe par P → X de V_{P/X}', the direct image of vertical vector fields, equal to End^0(E).
'fibré en Lie [?] associé' is likely 'fibré en algèbres de Lie associé'.
'est. [?] [-...-] ω par ω^2' is likely 'extension de ω par ω^2'.
'l'ens. de [?] relèvements' is likely 'l'ens. des relèvements'.
'torseur canonique sur S' may be 'sur X' (hard to read).
